experiment.title: Exact gatewise TT compilation of first-norm source advice
experiment.objective: Construct exact TT cores for the five fixed trace-zero first-norm source tensors directly from the frozen RCB arithmetic circuit without B^5 enumeration, independently replay every toy value and exact bond rank, and measure complete preprocessing, retained advice, target specialization, traffic, and peak-state costs.
controls: rank-one separable exact addition and Hadamard products
asymmetric synthetic TT with exact ranks (1,2,3,4)
general-basis XY source emitted but excluded from trace-zero retained advice
independent direct RCB enumeration in the verifier only
independent_variables: curve instance and registry size B
RCB addition stage and scalar gate

primary: producer full-tuple enumeration and prior-table read counts
independent source and target semantic mismatch counts
emitted TT bond dimensions versus independent exact unfolding ranks
per-gate raw and exact bond dimensions
maximum local factorization matrix and TT object words
fixed-curve preprocessing field operations and logical traffic
retained five-source advice words and canonical bytes
per-target coefficient, linear-combination, and recompression work
secondary: streamed Hadamard transfer dimensions and traffic
diagnostic core words separated from retained advice
verifier-only B^5 tuple evaluations and RCB calls
peak resident memory and peak live field words
wall-clock time by cell, operation, and gate
special modulus, curve, generator, registry, and target structure
rho and prior B^5 comparator boundaries reported without an exponent claim

stopping_rules: Stop and preserve the first cell if any semantic or shape invariant fails.
Stop before allocating a local factorization matrix or TT object above 1000000 field words.
Stop before any predicted or observed process allocation can exceed 2 GiB RSS.
Stop and invalidate the producer partition if a B^5 tuple path or prior full tensor is reached.
Stop and require a versioned protocol repair if an inherited manifest or RCB gate hash changes.
Do not stop merely because exact toy ranks saturate an ambient B or B^2 boundary.
invalidation_rules: Any curve, registry, target, mode order, tree, gate, sample, control, or mutation is selected after observing compiler ranks.
The producer enumerates five physical indices, reads a prior B^5 source table, or constructs cores from full tensor values.
The generator and verifier import a common TT evaluator, RCB routine, rank routine, tuple iterator, target coefficient routine, or accounting calculator.
Any floating-point rank, SVD, tolerance, approximate rounding, or probabilistic sketch affects an emitted core.
Raw bond products are labeled exact ranks or discarded without accounting.
Factorization matrices, copies, transfers, direct sums, retained cores, failed gates, logical traffic, canonical bytes, or peak state are omitted.
Verifier exhaustive work is reclassified as preprocessing advice or online work.
A semantic match alone is called exact recompression without independent bond-rank equality.
A first-norm compiler is described as a zero locator, relation algorithm, ECDLP break, or sub-rho result.
experiment.success_criterion: All six source-compilation cells and 18 target-specialization cells complete with zero producer full-tuple enumerations, zero prior-table reads, zero independent semantic mismatches, exact equality between every emitted nonzero bond and its independent unfolding rank, all 12 mutations rejected, complete preprocessing/advice/online/verification ledgers, and every allocation, matrix, TT object, traffic ceiling, RSS value, and runtime below its frozen reviewed gate.
experiment.falsification_criterion: A valid semantic mismatch rejects the affected circuit or TT operation; a valid bond mismatch rejects the exact-recompression claim; hidden enumeration or missing accounting invalidates the compiler evidence; and a resource stop weakens only the literal gatewise schedule at the first preserved gate and does not reject other exact TT or coefficient-space constructions.
